title: CSV to LaTeX Table Converter – Free, No Upload | OpenAnyDoc
description: Convert a CSV file into a LaTeX tabular with \hline rules and every special character escaped, ready to paste into a paper or thesis. Nothing uploaded.
heading: CSV to LaTeX Table
subtitle: Drop a CSV and get a LaTeX tabular at once, special characters escaped, ready to paste or download.
intro: Put experiment results or survey data into a paper, thesis or report without typing ampersands and backslashes by hand. Choose, drop or paste a CSV or TSV file and a LaTeX tabular appears at once: one l column per CSV column, \hline rules, the header row first, then one line per row. The characters LaTeX treats as commands, & % $ # _ { } ~ ^ and \, are escaped so the table compiles. The delimiter and encoding are detected for you, and the file is read in your browser, never uploaded.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your CSV is turned into LaTeX by your own browser and never sent to a server, so unpublished results stay on your device.

features.title: Compiles first time
features.text: & % $ # _ { } ~ ^ and \ in your data are escaped, so a value such as 50% or R&D does not break the build.

features.title: Works offline
features.text: Once this page has loaded, it keeps working without an internet connection.

stepsTitle: How it works: convert CSV to a LaTeX table

steps.title: Add your CSV
steps.text: Choose or drop a .csv or .tsv file, paste CSV text into the box, or try a sample.

steps.title: Get the tabular
steps.text: The tabular environment is written at once, with an l column per CSV column and \hline around the header.

steps.title: Paste it into your document
steps.text: Copy the code into your .tex file, inside a table environment if you want a caption, or download it as a .tex file.

handlesTitle: What the CSV to LaTeX converter handles
handles: Files: .csv and .tsv, or CSV text you paste; comma, semicolon, tab and pipe delimiters.
Output: a tabular with column spec l per column, \hline rules and the header row first.
Escaping: & % $ # _ { } ~ ^ and \ written as LaTeX-safe commands.
Quoted CSV fields with commas inside, as Excel and Google Sheets export them.
Encodings: UTF-8, UTF-16 and Windows-1256 Arabic, detected automatically.
limits: Arabic text needs XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX with an Arabic font (polyglossia or babel); the page does not set that up for you.
Every column is left-aligned (l); change the spec to r or c, or to siunitx S columns, for numbers.
The output is the tabular only: add \begin{table}, \caption and \label yourself.
faqTitle: CSV to LaTeX: questions and answers

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your browser reads the CSV and writes the LaTeX on your device. Pasted text stays in this tab and is never sent anywhere.

faq.question: Which characters are escaped?
faq.answer: The ten that LaTeX reads as commands: & % $ # _ { } ~ ^ and \. Each is written in its LaTeX-safe form, so 50% prints as 50% instead of starting a comment.

faq.question: Can I use it with Arabic data?
faq.answer: The text is written as it is, but pdfLaTeX cannot typeset Arabic. Compile with XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX and load an Arabic font through polyglossia or babel; the page does not add that setup.

faq.question: How do I align number columns to the right?
faq.answer: Every column is written as l. Change a letter in the column spec, for example {lrr}, to right-align those columns.

faq.question: Does it add a caption and label?
faq.answer: No. It writes the tabular only, so you can put it inside your own table environment with the caption, label and placement you use.

faq.question: Does it work with semicolon-separated files?
faq.answer: Yes. The delimiter is detected from the file, whether it is a comma, semicolon, tab or pipe.

faq.question: How do I convert a CSV file to a LaTeX table?
faq.answer: Open or paste the CSV, then copy the tabular code into your .tex document or download it as a .tex file. OpenAnyDoc escapes the characters LaTeX treats as commands and works in your browser, without uploading the data.
